campaigns.context: Hundreds of subdomains across 10 numerically-patterned apex domains (014901490149f/h/i/j/w/x/y/z.com and www01490243/58dd.com) embed a baidu label plus a date token in each subdomain name, consistent with Baidu brand impersonation or search-engine abuse. All apex domains were reported by a single researcher on 2026-08-04 with over 280 combined IOCs. The shared numeric-suffix naming pattern indicates coordinated infrastructure provisioning by a single actor.
campaigns.name: Baidu phishing wave on 014901490149* family domains

campaigns.context: Subdomains on catex.at and locaz.icu serve phishing pages at the path /cnbcard/web_sms_activate.php, consistent with a fake card activation flow that harvests SMS one-time passwords. The shared path structure across two unrelated apex domains indicates a common phishing kit deployed on multiple hosts. One researcher reported 19 IOCs on 2026-08-04.
campaigns.name: Bank card SMS activation phishing on catex.at and locaz.icu

campaigns.context: Multiple domains impersonate Telegram using deliberate misspellings - telergam-cdn* subdomains on aa9977rt.com, telegramtghg.com.cn, and fi-telegram.hl.cn - to host phishing pages. The Chinese-registered domains (.com.cn, .hl.cn) and date tokens in subdomain names suggest a focus on Chinese-speaking users. A single researcher reported all three clusters on 2026-08-04.
campaigns.name: Telegram impersonation phishing on typosquat domains

campaigns.context: Twelve IP addresses tagged as Evilginx adversary-in-the-middle phishing infrastructure were reported by Team Cymru S2 on 2026-08-06. Evilginx proxies legitimate login pages to intercept credentials and session cookies, bypassing multi-factor authentication. The IPs span multiple hosting providers and geographic regions, indicating distributed phishing campaign infrastructure.
campaigns.name: Evilginx adversary-in-the-middle phishing IP cluster

campaigns.context: A ClickFix social engineering campaign uses fake landing pages on getpixeltap.com and siege-close.com, plus a Cloudflare R2 bucket, to deliver malware with two known SHA256 hashes. A C2 IP at 31.76.87.37 responds on ports 80 and 8443. Four researchers reported 12 IOCs on 2026-08-07.
campaigns.name: ClickFix malware delivery via getpixeltap.com and siege-close.com

campaigns.context: Four .cfd domains - vokser.cfd, rdwksm.cfd, vorlen.cfd, and qbnzgt.cfd - serve phishing redirect pages where Cloudflare IP addresses are embedded directly in the URL path after a short token, for example /Ek41lT172.67.157.36CAPTCHA. The CAPTCHA suffix in some paths suggests a fake human-verification lure. Multiple researchers reported combined IOCs on 2026-08-03.
campaigns.name: Phishing on .cfd domains with IP embedded in URL path

campaigns.context: Phishing pages at /jmFfvPRN/ appear on five compromised legitimate hosts - urbanizab2b.com (Spanish B2B), vignobles-lorgeril.com (French winery), angels-travel.com, caixacat.com, and geek-asylum.com. An /ip endpoint variant suggests victim IP geolocation or filtering to serve targeted content. Three researchers reported 11 IOCs between 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-07.
campaigns.name: Phishing kit on compromised legitimate sites via /jmFfvPRN/ path

campaigns.context: Sliver C2 framework is distributed via multiple GitHub repositories using lookalike organization names, with C2 endpoints at c2.ashveil.org and 43.157.204.73. A fake ColdCard cryptocurrency wallet page (github.com/newallyson/ColdCard) is linked as a lure, and multiple ephemeral GitHub paths (dcm1-*, dm1-*) suggest ongoing infrastructure churn. Four researchers reported 11 IOCs between 2026-08-02 and 2026-08-07.
campaigns.name: Sliver C2 distributed via GitHub lookalike repositories

campaigns.context: Nine Android malware samples linked to a Pastebin raw URL (pastebin.com/raw/uh8JXav2) are tagged as Android Trojan. The distinct MD5 hashes suggest active repackaging or multiple payload variants staged at the same URL. Three researchers reported 10 IOCs between 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-06.
campaigns.name: Android Trojan distributed via Pastebin staging URL

campaigns.context: RemcosRAT samples are staged at cinnamonthai.com under /cgi-bins/ with versioned filenames (e.g. 05.08_8080_64.exe) and use DuckDNS hostnames careerlongprofit.duckdns.org and comeforreealz.duckdns.org plus tomwim.ygto.com as C2 endpoints. Two payload MD5 hashes are known. D3LabIT reported 10 IOCs between 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-07.
campaigns.name: RemcosRAT distributed via cinnamonthai.com and DuckDNS C2

campaigns.context: Phishing pages at /secure/secured.php appear on four domains - anfrgroup.com, dreamstravelandtour.com, microsharp.net, and mostaqpal-masr.com - a mix of likely compromised legitimate sites spanning multiple countries. The consistent path structure across unrelated hosts suggests a shared phishing kit. Kb4Threatlabs reported 8 IOCs on 2026-08-07.
campaigns.name: Phishing kit at /secure/secured.php on compromised hosts

campaigns.context: Eight IP addresses - a near-consecutive block of 188.127.246.70 through 188.127.246.76 plus 151.243.113.23 - are tagged as Magecart payment-card skimmer infrastructure. The tight sequential IP range suggests a single hosting customer provisioning dedicated skimmer back-end capacity. Team Cymru S2 reported 8 IOCs on 2026-08-04.
campaigns.name: Magecart skimmer C2 IP cluster

campaigns.context: Phishing pages at /MS/main/RBS/loginUsername on ra-kusdoawds.com and ra-posadwad.com impersonate Royal Bank of Scotland online banking login. The ra- prefix and shared path structure across both domains suggest a common phishing kit deployment on dedicated infrastructure. Two researchers reported 8 IOCs between 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-07.
campaigns.name: Royal Bank of Scotland login phishing on ra-* domains

campaigns.context: Phishing pages are hosted via IP-encoded subdomains on GoDaddy's secureserver.net (e.g. 93.105.205.92.host.secureserver.net), serving content at /vendas.html (Portuguese for 'sales') and /pdfPDF. Using a trusted registrar's shared hosting domain reduces domain-reputation blocking effectiveness. One researcher reported 8 IOCs on 2026-08-07.
campaigns.name: Phishing on GoDaddy secureserver.net via IP-encoded subdomains

campaigns.context: Phishing pages at /login paths on dslkk.cn, niuaniu.top, and raaglpfplzp.top target Japanese bank customers, consistent with Resona Bank impersonation. The uniform /login path across geographically diverse hosts is consistent with a shared phishing kit. Two researchers reported 6 IOCs between 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-07.
campaigns.name: Resona Bank phishing via /login pages

campaigns.context: Three randomized subdomains on edgeone.dev, Tencent's edge cloud platform, are tagged as phishing pages and were active from 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-07. Hosting phishing on legitimate cloud infrastructure reduces the effectiveness of domain-based blocking. One reporter flagged 6 IOCs with no identified targeted brand.
campaigns.name: Phishing hosted on Tencent EdgeOne cloud platform

campaigns.context: Open directories on dokument-pdf.lat and nfexmlfiscal.com.br (subdomains dnf and xml) expose Brazilian Nota Fiscal Eletronica invoice-themed files, consistent with malware delivery via fake e-invoice lures. The uniform /files/ path and NF-e subdomain naming across unrelated domains suggest a shared deployment kit targeting Brazilian users. JAMESWT_WT reported 6 IOCs on 2026-08-05.
campaigns.name: Brazilian NF-e invoice lure via open directory

campaigns.context: The domain jpword.cc and subdomain agent.jpword.cc serve a /setup.pdf file suggesting a document lure for malware delivery, with jpword.cc also accessible on port 8383 as a likely C2 endpoint. Two researchers reported 5 IOCs on 2026-08-06.
campaigns.name: Malware delivery via jpword.cc with /setup.pdf lure

campaigns.context: Subdomains smtp.hostinger.com and c2smtp.hostinger.com on port 587 appear in IOC feeds as command-and-control SMTP channels. The c2smtp subdomain label directly indicates malicious use, likely data exfiltration or bot tasking routed through legitimate Hostinger email infrastructure to evade IP-based blocking. Two researchers reported 5 IOCs on 2026-08-06.
campaigns.name: C2 SMTP channel via Hostinger mail infrastructure

campaigns.context: Subdomains a2 and e1 on cdnresolver.com are tagged as stealer command-and-control endpoints. The domain name mimics a legitimate CDN resolver service to blend malicious traffic with routine network infrastructure lookups. One researcher reported 4 IOCs on 2026-08-04.
campaigns.name: Stealer C2 infrastructure on cdnresolver.com
